checks: Source 39ba6f71d6fbae25:01 §§1–3, (1)–(3) gives strict containment, independent perturbation and perpendicular thickening. The realized body need not be strictly convex.

An excluded-target representation has at least two distinct positively weighted bases, so strict convexity makes their lifted partial interpolation interior. Positive weighting with the remaining points retains interiority and hence own-fiber interiority. This also rules out excluded-target representations at zero-volume sites.

Each compact interpolant at an extreme coefficient vector has a positive distance to the complement. Finitely many extremes give a uniform positive margin, and the support-function inequality is affine in the coefficients and hence extends to every representation. Weighted source Hausdorff errors and target error each cost at most epsilon, leaving positive slack.

Representations using the target can be reduced to the excluded-target representation by removing its coefficient and renormalizing unless that coefficient is one. This is the exact anchored hypothesis in ba0f3db1bf4f62c6. The hull projection has no extra integer points because it lies inside the original projection and P is the complete old integer base list.

A positive fiber supplies all continuous directions and lifted base differences supply the base direction space E. Small perpendicular thickening completes the affine span. There are finitely many candidate integer bases in a fixed bounded enlargement, and choosing the radius smaller than their positive distances from aff P excludes every new exterior-affine base. At a base in aff P the perpendicular displacement must vanish, preserving all exact sections.

dependencies.hypotheses: The finite base set is nonempty, every perturbed or retained fiber is compact convex and nonempty, and all anchored Minkowski inclusions are proved. The accepted equivalence therefore identifies the exact sections of their placed hull, including zero-volume retained fibers. No positive-volume assumption from that fact's later depth comparison is needed for the equivalence.

overlap.comparison: It gives the same openness step for full-rank bases with all fibers positive under an assumed strict compatibility condition. The new result derives strict compatibility from ambient strict convexity, keeps null fibers, and constructs a full-dimensional realization at deficient base span.
It uses strict compatibility as a hypothesis for ambient exposure of own support points. It neither derives the margin from strict ambient convexity nor proves perturbation stability.

readability: The excluded-target condition is essential to a uniform positive margin. The proof properly uses separate convexity to reinsert the target coefficient.
review_method: Independent frozen-proof read, source comparison, and predecessor audit
summary: Strict ambient convexity gives a uniform excluded-target interpolation margin and stable exact fibers, including the null-site and deficient-base-span cases.
